question: In 2025, Mumbai Marathon was held in which month?
solution:
The correct answer is __**January**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mumbai Marathon** is one of the most popular and prestigious marathon events held annually in **India**, attracting runners from across the globe.
 
• Since its inception in **2004**, the Mumbai Marathon has traditionally been held in the month of **January**. This is due to favorable weather conditions during this time of the year.
 
• The event is typically scheduled on a **Sunday** in mid-January to facilitate maximum participation and minimize disruption to city activities.
 
• January is considered ideal for running long distances in Mumbai as the temperature during this period is generally cool, ranging from **16°C to 24°C**, which enhances runner performance and comfort.
 
• The event includes various categories such as **Full Marathon**, **Half Marathon**, **Dream Run**, and **Senior Citizen Run**, making it accessible to participants of all ages and abilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History and Significance:**

 
 
• The **Mumbai Marathon** was launched in **2004** and has since grown into one of the largest and most prestigious marathons in Asia.
 
• It is organized by **Procam International** and is sponsored by leading corporations, ensuring professional execution and high standards.
 
• The event promotes health, fitness, and community participation, while also serving as a platform for raising funds for various charitable causes. Since its inception, it has raised millions for charity.
 
 
 
• **Venue and Route:**
 
 
• The marathon route offers participants a scenic view of Mumbai, including iconic landmarks like the **Marine Drive**, **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus**, and the **Sea Link**.
 
• The race starts and ends at the **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus** and passes through various areas of the city.
 
 
 
• **Participation and Categories:**
 
 
• The marathon attracts participants from across the globe, including elite runners, amateur athletes, and fitness enthusiasts.
 
• Categories include the **Full Marathon (42.195 km)**, **Half Marathon (21.097 km)**, **Dream Run (6 km)**, and **Senior Citizen Run**.
 
• The event also includes a **Champions with Disability Run**, promoting inclusivity and participation for differently-abled individuals.
 
 
 
• **Weather Considerations:**
 
 
• January is one of the coolest months in Mumbai, with temperatures ranging from **16°C to 24°C**, providing ideal conditions for marathon runners.
 
• Humidity is also relatively lower in January compared to other months, ensuring better endurance and performance for participants.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• The Mumbai Marathon is recognized by global organizations such as the **World Athletics** and attracts elite athletes who compete for prize money.
 
• It is part of the prestigious **Abbott World Marathon Majors**, showcasing its significance in the global marathon calendar.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Charity Impact:**

 
 
• The Mumbai Marathon is a major platform for fundraising, with hundreds of NGOs participating to raise funds for various causes.
 
• In 2020 alone, the event raised over **₹32 crore**, benefiting numerous charitable organizations.
 
 
 
• **COVID-19 Adaptations:**
 
 
• During the **COVID-19 pandemic**, the marathon adopted virtual formats to ensure continuity while adhering to safety protocols.
 
• Participants were encouraged to run in their local areas and submit their results online.
 
 
 
• **Elite Participation:**
 
 
• Every year, elite athletes from Kenya, Ethiopia, and other nations participate, showcasing their prowess in distance running.
 
• The event provides an opportunity for Indian runners to compete alongside international athletes and gain exposure.
